title: Phases of Matter
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Phases of Matter Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Matter has mass, takes up space and can change phase: solids, liquids and gases change with heating (melting, boiling) and cooling (freezing, condensing); these physical changes are reversible and depend on particle motion. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 4, Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets (BC): solids, liquids and gases, melting, freezing, boiling, condensation, and particles and heat. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Heating or cooling can change the phase of matter.
key_sub: Melting, freezing, boiling and condensing can be undone.
body_html:
How to think about it

Matter exists as solid, liquid or gas. Heating makes particles move faster: a solid melts into a liquid, and a liquid boils or evaporates into a gas. Cooling slows them: a gas condenses into a liquid, and a liquid freezes into a solid.

These are physical changes: the substance is still the same (ice, water and steam are all water), so they can be reversed. Water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C.

Example

What happens to water vapour on a cold window?

It cools down.

Answer: it condenses into drops

Example

Is melting ice a physical or chemical change?

It is still water.

Answer: physical

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the bubbles in boiling water are air (they are water vapour).
  • Thinking a substance gets heavier when it freezes.
  • Mixing up evaporation and condensation.

items.q: Is lemonade a solid, a liquid or a gas?
items.e: Lemonade is a liquid.

items.q: Which of these is a gas?
items.e: A gas has no definite shape and no definite volume.

items.q: Which of these is a liquid?
items.e: A liquid has a definite volume but no definite shape.

items.q: Which states of matter cannot be squashed into a smaller space?
items.e: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow; gases spread out and can be squashed.

items.q: Which state of matter keeps its own shape?
items.e: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow; gases spread out and can be squashed.

items.q: What is matter?
c: anything that has mass and takes up space
items.e: Air is matter too.

items.q: Which state of matter escapes from an open container?
items.e: Solids keep their shape; liquids flow; gases spread out and can be squashed.

items.q: Which state of matter flows and takes the shape of its container?

items.q: Is helium in a balloon a solid, a liquid or a gas?

items.q: Is sugar a solid, a liquid or a gas?

items.q: Which state of matter has a fixed shape and a fixed volume?

items.q: Is the bubbles in a pop a solid, a liquid or a gas?

items.q: Which of these is a solid?

items.q: Which property describes how easily a material bends without breaking?

items.q: Which state of matter forms a puddle when spilt?
